
The PSHA combines the probabilities of all earthquake scenarios with predictions of resulting ground motion intensity, as described in previous sections. To identify the contributing events for a given ground motion intensity and AEP (or return period), the seismic hazard deaggregation computes the relative contribution of earthquake parameters magnitude $M$ and distance $R$ to the total hazard. The full deaggregation methodology can be found in references @Kramer1997, @Bazzurro1999 . Conceptually, the contribution of a magnitude $\bar{m}$ and distance $\bar{r}$ to the total hazard can be obtained from the Bayes' theorem from the total and marginal AEP :

$$\bar{m}=m_l \ \ \ ;\ \ \  l \in \mathrm{max}\left[ \dfrac{\lambda[I>i^\ast|M=m_1]}{\lambda_I(i^\ast)},..,\dfrac{\lambda[I>i^\ast|M=m_k]}{\lambda_I(i^\ast)}..,\dfrac{\lambda[I>i^\ast|M=m_N]}{\lambda_I(i^\ast)}\right]$$ {#eq-DIS1}

$$ \bar{r}=r_l \ \ \ ;\ \ \ l \in \mathrm{max}\left[ \dfrac{\lambda[I>i^\ast|R=r_1]}{\lambda_I(i^\ast)},..,\dfrac{\lambda[I>i^\ast|R=r_j]}{\lambda_I(i^\ast)},..,\dfrac{\lambda[I>i^\ast|R=r_N]}{\lambda_I(i^\ast)} \right]$$ {#eq-DIS2}

where $\lambda[I>i^\ast]$ is the total AEP for all sources defined before, and $\lambda[I>i^\ast|M=m_u]$ and $\lambda[I>i^\ast|R=r_v]$ are the marginal probabilities for events of magnitude $\bar{m}$ and distance $\bar{r}$

$$
\lambda[I>i^\ast|M=m_u]\simeq \sum_{N_S}\nu_o^{(s)}\sum_{N_R}\sum_{N_M}\Phi_C^{(s)} (\varepsilon_{j,k}^\ast)f_M^{(s)}(\bar{m})\,\Delta m f_{R|M}^{(s)}(r_k|m_u)\Delta r
$$ {#eq-DIS3}

$$\lambda[I>i^\ast|R=r_v]\simeq \sum_{N_S}\nu_o^{(s)} \sum_{N_R}\sum_{N_M}\Phi_C^{(s)} (\varepsilon_{j,k}^\ast)f_M^{(s)}(m_j)\,\Delta m f_{R|M}^{(s)}(r_v|m_j)\Delta r$$ {#eq-DIS4}

With this procedure, the fractional contribution of different subsets of the events with respect to the total hazard is computed. The deaggregation by magnitude and distance bins allows the dominant scenario earthquake (M-R bins) to be identified. When several mechanisms contribute to the total hazard, the deaggregation procedure can be performed for a family of sources and identify the M-R bins for each mechanism, allowing the identification of the dominant seismic source. In a probabilistic framework, the magnitude-distance bins $M_w-R$ that control the seismic hazard is defined as the *controlling scenario* for a given target AEP and structural period $T_n$.
